sprints.title: Unified Notification Convergence: Server + Web Push + Android FCM + Firebase
sprints.goal: Harmonize every existing Kairo notification mechanism into one coherent notification platform while preserving the strongest parts of the existing implementation. Not a greenfield implementation.
tasks: Preserve and consolidate: authenticated tenant-scoped inbox, NotificationDevice, NotificationDeviceProfile, WebPushSubscription, FirebasePushSubscription, NotificationOutboxEvent, VAPID Web Push, Android FCM registration, Firebase Admin backend delivery, Flutter FCM token refresh, Flutter permission flow, background Android delivery, deep links, Celery outbox worker, preferences, finance/discipline/announcement/event categories.
Never hardcode sender IDs, API credentials or service-account keys. Never commit google-services.json, Firebase Admin service account JSON, private VAPID key, FCM credentials.

Architecture target: Business operation -> Domain Event -> Notification Policy / Recipient Resolver -> Transactional Notification Outbox -> Authenticated Inbox and Delivery Dispatcher -> Web Push VAPID and Android FCM -> Browser and Firebase V1 -> authenticated deep link.
Authenticated inbox is the source of detailed notification information; push transports are delivery hints.
Sensitive push content policy: never expose finance or disciplinary details on a lock screen; generic default body; safe internal target only.

Canonical notification envelope: notification_id, event_id, tenant_id, recipient_user_id, category, priority, event_type, target_path, created_at, deduplication_key, correlation_id, metadata, push_policy.

Recipient resolution: audit existing event generation and document a notification-event matrix (producer, event, category, eligible recipients, inbox, Web Push, Android FCM, deep link, privacy level) for payment recorded, contribution/receipt declared, receipt validated, receipt rejected, cash handover required/completed, treasury receipt confirmed, expense recorded, disciplinary status update, announcement published, event published, security events.

Preferences: one canonical preference contract consumed by both clients; preserve backward compatibility; define user-wide vs tenant-user-wide vs device-profile-specific scope and prefer the safest model already represented by NotificationDeviceProfile.

Device registration: stable random installation ID never derived from account identity; every subscription tenant/user scoped; support multiple accounts on one device without cross-account push leakage.
Token rotation: FCM refresh updates safely, avoids duplicates, preserves tenant/user binding, disables obsolete tokens.
Logout/session revocation: logout stops authenticated notification handling; choose and test one clear model for profile binding vs installation identity.
Invalid token handling: permanently invalid/unregistered tokens are disabled; transient errors use bounded retry with backoff.
Web Push: keep standards-based Web Push + VAPID; do not migrate to Firebase merely for uniformity; transports are replaceable.
Web service worker: verify push reception, notification display, notification click, deep-link routing, expired subscription handling, unread count refresh.
Android states: verify foreground, background, terminated/cold-start where testable; taps route through authenticated navigation and never bypass authorization.
Deep links: restricted to safe internal Kairo destinations; never blindly navigate to arbitrary external URLs; route guards and backend permissions still apply.

Outbox: one business transaction creates its intended notification atomically; delivery failure never rolls back a committed business transaction; statuses pending/processing/delivered/failed/dead; maintain attempts and last error; prevent duplicate processing.

Observability metrics: notification_outbox_pending, notification_outbox_failed, notification_outbox_oldest_age, web_push_success, web_push_failure, fcm_success, fcm_failure, disabled_web_subscriptions, disabled_fcm_tokens; no notification contents in logs.

Operator notification health section: Web Push configured, Firebase configured, worker running, pending outbox count, failed deliveries, invalid subscriptions, last successful dispatch; never show private keys or tokens.

Testing: provider abstractions, deterministic fake Web Push and fake FCM providers, no real Firebase service account in CI; cover tenant isolation, device-profile isolation, deduplication, preference filtering, both dispatchers, invalid token disabling, transient retry, deep link validation, logout/session behavior, outbox retries, multiple accounts per device, one account on multiple devices, sensitive push content policy.
Optional opt-in live Firebase smoke test (npm run notifications:firebase:doctor or equivalent) that never runs in generic CI and prints only non-secret diagnostics.

Update the operator guide for Firebase project configuration, FCM API V1, Android package identity, Admin service account placement, Docker/worker secret mounts, environment configuration, token troubleshooting, physical device validation.
acceptance: One canonical notification pipeline exists.
Detailed notification data remains authenticated.
Web Push works through the same inbox/outbox model.
Android FCM works through the same inbox/outbox model.

Tenant isolation is tested.

Worker retries are bounded.
